subject: Chemistry
cards: AQA-7405.ENTHALPY_CHANGE

Define enthalpy change.

[1 mark]

heat (energy) change at constant pressure
Also accept: change in heat content at constant pressure
Ignore: reference to standard states
AQA-7405.ELECTRONEGATIVITY

Define electronegativity.

[1 mark]

• The (relative) ability of an atom to attract electron density in a covalent bond
• OR
• the (relative) ability of an atom to attract the pair of electrons in a covalent bond.
AQA-7405.RELATIVE_ATOMIC_MASS

Define the term relative atomic mass.

[2 marks]

• **average/mean mass of 1 atom (of an element)**
• 1/12 mass of one atom of 12C
• or
• **average/mean mass of atoms of an element**
• 1/12 mass of one atom of 12C
• or
• **average/mean mass of atoms of an element ×12**
• mass of one atom of 12C
• or
• **(average) mass of one mole of atoms**
• 1/12 mass of one mole of 12C
• or
• **(weighted) average mass of all the isotopes**
• 1/12 mass of one atom of 12C
• or
• average mass of an atom/isotope (compared to C-12) on a scale in which an atom of C-12 has a mass of 12
Note: if moles and atoms/isotopes mixed max = 1
AQA-7405.ELECTRON_IMPACT_IONISATION

State the meaning of the term electron impact ionisation.

[1 mark]
(High energy) electrons (from an electron gun) are used to knock out an electron (from each molecule or atom.)
AQA-7405.STRONG_ACID

State the meaning of the term strong acid.

[1 mark]
completely dissociates/ionises (to form H+ ions)
AQA-7405.WEAK_ACID

Propanoic acid is a weak acid. State the meaning of weak in this context.

[1 mark]

• only a (small) fraction of the molecules dissociate (into ions) / ionise (when added to water / in aqueous solution)
• OR
• partially dissociates / does not fully dissociate (into ions) / ionise (when added to water / in aqueous solution)
Not accepted: ‘reaction is reversible’
Not accepted: if incorrect ions suggested
Not accepted: “Hydrogen ions do not fully dissociate”
AQA-7405.PERIODICITY

State the meaning of the term periodicity.

[1 mark]

**Repeating** pattern/trends (of physical or chemical properties/reactions)
Also accept: named property
Note: Penalise groups
AQA-7405.TRANSITION_METAL_COMPLEX

State the meaning of the term transition metal complex.

[1 mark]

(Central) metal atom/ion surrounded by ligands
Also accept: complex in which number of coordinate bonds exceeds oxidation state of the metal
AQA-7405.PERFECT_IONIC_MODEL

State the meaning of the term perfect ionic model.

[1 mark]

• (Ions are) point charges
• Or
• (Ions are) perfect spheres
• Or
• No covalent character
Also accept: no polarisation of ions
Not accepted: atoms or molecules in answer
AQA-7405.MASS_NUMBER_OF_AN_ATOM

Define the mass number of an atom.

[1 mark]

**Number** of protons + neutrons (in the nucleus of the atom)
Not accepted: reference to mass or average
Ignore: references to C-12 being 12
AQA-7405.ELECTROCHEMICAL_SERIES

State the meaning of the term electrochemical series.

[1 mark]

• (List of) electrode potentials/Eo in (numerical) order
• OR half cells/equations in (numerical) order of electrode potential/Eo
Not accepted: EMF in order
AQA-7405.COMPLEMENTARY_WHEN_IT_IS_USED_TO_REFER_TO_DNA_STRANDS

State the meaning of the term complementary when it is used to refer to DNA strands.

[1 mark]

(Complementary means the two strands must have base sequences) that match (all) **A to T and C to G**
Ignore: reference to (hydrogen) bonding
AQA-7405.FRACTION_AS_USED_IN_THE_TERM_PETROL_FRACTION

State the meaning of fraction, as used in the term petrol fraction.

[1 mark]

A group of (hydrocarbons/compounds) with similar boiling points
Also accept: compounds that boil in a similar range of temperatures
Also accept: Compounds with similar (carbon) chain length with C5-C12 range or within range
AQA-7405.ENTHALPY_OF_LATTICE_DISSOCIATION

Define the term enthalpy of lattice dissociation.

[2 marks]

• The enthalpy change / ΔH when one mole of a (solid) ionic compound
• dissociates (fully) into gaseous ions
Also accept: heat change at constant pressure when...
Also accept: suitable equation with state symbols for ions
Not accepted: one mole of gaseous ions
Ignore: standard states / conditions
Ignore: heat change (alone) / energy change
AQA-7405.STEREOISOMERS

Define the term stereoisomers.

[2 marks]

• (Different molecules/compounds with the) same (molecular and) structural formula
• Different spatial arrangement of atoms
Also accept: different spatial arrangement of bonds/groups
AQA-7405.HETEROGENEOUS

State the meaning of the term heterogeneous.

[1 mark]

(catalyst is in) different phase/state (to reactants)
Also accept: ... to reactants and products
Not accepted: ... to products
AQA-7405.HETEROGENEOUS_CATALYST

State the meaning of the term heterogeneous catalyst.

[2 marks]

• Catalyst in different phase/state (to reactants)
• Speeds up reaction without being used up
Also accept: catalyst in different phase/state to reactants and products
Also accept: speeds up the reaction by (providing alternative route for reaction and) lowering Ea
Not accepted: (catalyst in different phase/state to) products
Not accepted: does not take part in the reaction
AQA-7405.R_3_1_10_KP_EXPRESSION_METHANOL

Give an expression for the equilibrium constant (Kp) for this reaction. CO(g) + 2 H2(g) <=> CH3OH(g)

[1 mark]

Kp = p(CH3OH) / p(H2)^2 p(CO)
Not accepted: square brackets
AQA-7405.R_3_1_10_KP_NO_UNITS

H2O(g) + CO(g) <=> H2(g) + CO2(g). State why the equilibrium constant (Kp) for this reaction has no units.

[1 mark]

(The amount in) moles of products is the same as reactants (so the units (of partial pressure) cancel out)
Also accept: equal moles/molecules/particles on both sides (so units cancel)
AQA-7405.R_3_1_10_KP_VOLUME_NO_EFFECT

H2O(g) + CO(g) <=> H2(g) + CO2(g). State the effect, if any, of an increase in volume of the container on the value of Kp for this reaction at a constant temperature.

[1 mark]
no effect
AQA-7405.R_3_1_2_WEIGH_SOLID_ACCURATE_MASS

Describe a method to add an accurately known mass of solid to a beaker to make a solution.

[2 marks]

• measure the mass of the weighing boat (or similar) and solid
• Add the solid to a beaker (or other suitable container) and then reweigh the weighing boat (and subtract to find the mass of solid added.)
• OR
• Place weighing boat on a balance and zero the balance
• Add the solid to a beaker (or other suitable container), wash out weighing boat and transfer washing to the beaker.
Also accept: M1 place (an empty) beaker on balance and zero
Also accept: M2 add the solid to the beaker and record the mass
Also accept: M1 place (an empty) beaker on balance and measure its mass
Also accept: M2 add the solid to the beaker and subtract mass of empty beaker from the total mass
AQA-7405.R_3_1_2_VOLUMETRIC_FLASK_MAKE_UP

The mass of barium hydroxide is dissolved in a beaker containing 150 cm3 of distilled water. Describe how this solution is used to make 250 cm3 of the 0.100 mol dm-3 barium hydroxide solution.

[3 marks]

• Transfers the solution to a **volumetric/graduated** flask
• Add **washings** using **distilled** water and make up to the graduation mark/250 cm3
• Invert many times / shake to mix
AQA-7405.R_3_1_2_RINSE_PIPETTE_WITH_SOLUTION

Before the first titration, the 25 cm3 pipette is rinsed with a small volume of the 0.100 mol dm-3 barium hydroxide solution. State why it is good practice to rinse the pipette in this way.

[1 mark]

So that the titration is done with known concentration of Ba(OH)2
Also accept: so that water does not dilute the solution
Also accept: remove water/prevent contamination
AQA-7405.R_3_1_5_CATALYST_HOW_RATE

Describe how a catalyst increases the rate of a reaction.

[2 marks]

• provides alternative route/mechanism/pathway
• with lower activation energy
AQA-7405.R_3_1_5_TEMPERATURE_RATE_EXPLAIN

Explain why the rate of a reaction increases as the temperature increases.

[3 marks]

• particles/molecules/reactants move faster / have greater (kinetic) energy
• more particles/molecules have (energy greater than/equal to) the activation energy
• successful collisions are more frequent
Also accept: per unit time for frequency
Ignore: atoms
Ignore: vibrations
AQA-7405.R_3_1_7_OXIDISING_AGENT_ELECTRONS

State, in terms of electrons, the meaning of the term oxidising agent.

[1 mark]

Electron acceptor / gains electrons
Not accepted: electron pair acceptor / gain of electrons
AQA-7405.R_3_1_7_HALF_EQ_CU_OXIDATION

Give a half-equation to show the oxidation of copper to copper(II) ions.

[1 mark]

Cu -> Cu2+ + 2e-
Also accept: multiples
Ignore: state symbols, even if incorrect.
AQA-7405.R_3_1_7_HALF_EQ_NITRATE_REDUCTION

Give a half-equation to show the reduction of NO3- ions in acidic solution to NO2

[1 mark]

NO3- + 2 H+ + e- -> NO2 + H2O
Also accept: multiples
Ignore: state symbols, even if incorrect.
AQA-7405.R_3_1_7_CR_PF3_OXIDATION_ZERO

Suggest why the oxidation state of chromium is zero in Cr(PF3)6

[1 mark]

PF3 is neutral **and** the complex is neutral
Also accept: PF3 has no charge and the complex has no charge
Ignore: electronegativity
AQA-7405.R_3_1_7_CALCIUM_WATER_REDOX

The reaction of calcium with water is a redox reaction. Explain, in terms of oxidation states, why this reaction involves both oxidation and reduction.

[2 marks]

• Oxidation state of Ca increases, so Ca is oxidised
• OR
• Oxidation state of Ca from 0 to +2, so Ca is oxidised
• Oxidation state of H decreases, so H is reduced
• OR
• Oxidation state of H from +1 to 0, so H is reduced
Also accept: If no marks awarded, then correct oxidation states of Ca **and** H before **and** after the reaction scores 1 mark
AQA-7405.R_3_2_2_MG_TICL4_EQUATION_ROLE

Give an equation for the reaction between titanium(IV) chloride and magnesium. State the role of magnesium in this reaction.

[2 marks]

• 2 Mg + TiCl4 -> Ti + 2 MgCl2
• Reducing agent
Also accept: multiples / ignore ss
Also accept: electron donor (not electron pair donor)
AQA-7405.R_3_2_2_DISTINGUISH_NACL_BACL2

The following pairs of compounds, each in aqueous solution, can be distinguished by simple test-tube reactions. Give a reagent, or combination of reagents, that can be added to the solutions in each pair to distinguish between them in a single reaction. State what is observed in each case. NaCl(aq) and BaCl2(aq)

[3 marks]

• Reagent: H2SO4 / Na2SO4 / any soluble sulfate
• Observation with NaCl: no (visible) change
• Observation with BaCl2: white ppt / white solid formed
Also accept: "no reaction","nvc","no change";
Not accepted: "nothing","no observation" and observations by omission (e.g. no ppt)
Ignore: conc for H2SO4
Note: If reagent incorrect then cannot score observations
Note: If reagent incomplete (e.g. SO4 2-), then lose M1 but mark on
AQA-7405.R_3_2_2_GROUP2_FIRST_IE_DECREASE

Explain why the first ionisation energy of the group 2 elements decreases down the group.

[2 marks]

• the outer electron is in a higher (energy) level / there is an increase in shielding / the atoms get larger / more shells
• There is a weaker attraction between the nucleus and the outer electron.
AQA-7405.R_3_2_2_GROUP2_ATOMIC_RADIUS_TREND

State the trend in the atomic radius of the elements down group 2 from Mg to Ba. Give a reason for this trend.

[2 marks]

• Trend: increases
• Reason: the number of electron energy levels increases
Also accept: the number of electron shells increases
Ignore: increase in shielding
AQA-7405.R_3_2_2_CA_RADIUS_GREATER_THAN_MG

State why the atomic radius of calcium is greater than the atomic radius of magnesium.

[1 mark]

• more shells
• Or
• more energy levels
Also accept: Ca has 4 shells and Mg has 3 shells
Not accepted: more outer shells
Ignore: shielding
Ignore: subshells/orbitals/more electrons
AQA-7405.R_3_2_2_MG_STEAM_EQUATION_OBSERVATIONS

Give an equation, including state symbols, for the reaction of magnesium with steam. State two observations for this reaction.

[3 marks]

• Mg(s) + H2O(g) -> MgO(s) + H2(g)
• Bright/white flame/light
• White/grey ash/powder (allow smoke)
Not accepted: ppt
Ignore: black solid
Ignore: fumes.
Note: State symbols essential
AQA-7405.R_3_2_2_MG_STEAM_OBSERVATION_EQUATION

State one observation when magnesium reacts with steam. Give an equation, including state symbols, for this reaction.

[2 marks]

• Bright light / white light / white powder/ash/solid
• Mg(s) + H2O(g) -> MgO(s) + H2(g)
Note: State symbols essential
AQA-7405.R_3_2_2_MG_STEAM_EQUATION_ONLY

Magnesium reacts with steam. Give an equation, including state symbols, for this reaction.

[1 mark]

Mg(s) + H2O(g) -> MgO(s) + H2(g)
Also accept: multiples
Note: State symbols required
AQA-7405.R_3_2_2_LEAST_SOLUBLE_GROUP2_SULFATE

The sulfates of the elements in group 2 from Mg to Ba have different solubilities. State the formula of the least soluble of these sulfates. Give a use for this sulfate.

[2 marks]

• BaSO4
• X-rays (of internal organs) / barium meal
AQA-7405.R_3_2_2_BASO4_HOSPITAL_PROPERTY

Give one property of barium sulfate that makes it useful in hospitals.

[1 mark]

• Insoluble
• OR
• Shows up on/blocks/absorbs/scatters X-ray
• OR
• Radiopaque
Ignore: barium meal if no qualification
Ignore: X-rays if no qualification
AQA-7405.R_3_2_2_MG_COLD_WATER_VS_STEAM

Magnesium reacts slowly with cold water but rapidly with steam. Compare these reactions, in terms of the products formed. You should identify one similarity in, and one difference between, these reactions.

[2 marks]

• Similarity: produce hydrogen / produce gas / produce white solids / produce Mg2+ compounds / produce a base
• Difference: magnesium oxide formed with steam and magnesium hydroxide formed with (cold) water
AQA-7405.R_3_2_2_BA_WATER_EQUATION

Give an equation, including state symbols, for the reaction between barium and water.

[1 mark]

Ba(s) + 2 H2O(l) -> Ba(OH)2(aq) + H2(g)
Also accept: multiples
Also accept: ionic equation
Note: State symbols essential
AQA-7405.R_3_2_2_GROUP2_LOWEST_SECOND_IE

This question is about the group 2 metals Mg to Ba. Identify the group 2 metal with the lowest second ionisation energy.

[1 mark]

Ba (barium)
Also accept: Ra (radium)
AQA-7405.R_3_2_2_MG_HYDROXIDE_MEDICAL_USE

Give one medical use for magnesium hydroxide.

[1 mark]

Indigestion relief / laxative / neutralise (excess stomach) acid
Also accept: milk of magnesia
AQA-7405.R_3_2_2_MG_HYDROXIDE_SAFER_THAN_NAOH

Magnesium hydroxide is used to relieve the symptoms of indigestion by neutralising stomach acid. Suggest why magnesium hydroxide is safer than sodium hydroxide as a treatment for indigestion.

[1 mark]

• magnesium hydroxide is insoluble/sparingly soluble/less soluble (than sodium hydroxide)
• OR
• magnesium hydroxide is less/not corrosive (but sodium hydroxide is corrosive)
Ignore: references to base strength or pH
AQA-7405.R_3_2_2_MG_EXPENSIVE_WHY

Titanium is an expensive metal because its extraction process uses magnesium. Suggest why magnesium is expensive.

[1 mark]

• The process to extract magnesium uses a lot of energy
• OR
• The extraction uses electrolysis
AQA-7405.R_3_1_2_ATOM_ECONOMY_ECONOMIC_ADVANTAGE

Suggest one economic advantage of using a process with a high percentage atom economy.

[1 mark]

• Idea of maximising the mass of reactants/atoms that ends up in the useful products
• OR
• Idea of minimising waste / biproduct (to be disposed of)
Not accepted: it costs less unless qualified.
Ignore: references to yield and energy
AQA-7405.R_3_3_14_FEWER_STEPS_ATOM_ECONOMY_AIM

Suggest why chemists usually aim to design production methods
- with fewer steps
- with a high percentage atom economy.

[2 marks]

• Less energy used **OR** Better yield
• Less waste **OR** Less pollution
Also accept: reduces practical losses, simpler plant,
Also accept: maximises the use of raw materials in the process into useful products, saves resources
AQA-7405.R_3_2_3_HALOGEN_ELECTRONEGATIVITY_DECREASES

Explain why the electronegativity of the halogens decreases down the group.

[2 marks]

• Larger atoms / more electron shells / more shielding / bonding pair of electrons further from the nucleus
• weaker attraction between nucleus and bonding pair of electrons / weaker attraction between nucleus and shared pair of electrons / weaker attraction between nucleus and electron density in the covalent bond
Ignore: references to outer electrons
AQA-7405.R_3_2_3_NACL_NABR_CONC_H2SO4_COMPARE

Concentrated sulfuric acid reacts with solid sodium chloride and with solid sodium bromide. State one similarity in, and one difference between, these reactions.

[2 marks]

• Similarity: one from
• form hydrogen halides / undergo acid-base reaction / misty white fumes are observed / form sodium sulfate / form sodium hydrogensulfate / exothermic / effervescence
• Difference: one from
• bromide undergoes a redox reaction / bromide ions are oxidised / bromide ions reduce sulfur in sulfuric acid / red-brown-orange fumes are observed with bromide / Br2 produced with bromide / (choking gas) SO2 produced with bromide / different hydrogen halides
AQA-7405.R_3_2_3_CHLORINE_DRINKING_WATER_WHY_SAFE

Chlorine is toxic but is added to drinking water. State why chlorine is added to drinking water. Explain why this is safe to do even though chlorine is toxic.

[2 marks]

• Kill bacteria / to prevent water-borne diseases / to prevent people getting cholera / to sterilise water
• Small enough concentration (to avoid harming humans)
Also accept: any named bacterial (water-borne) infection.
AQA-7405.R_3_2_3_CHLORINE_AMOUNT_CONTROLLED

Chlorine is added to some drinking water supplies to decrease the risk of people suffering from diseases such as cholera. State why the amount of chlorine added must be controlled.

[1 mark]
toxic/poisonous/too much chlorine causes death
AQA-7405.R_3_2_3_CHLORINE_WATER_TREATMENT_THREE

Chlorine is used to treat water even though it is toxic to humans. Give one reason why water is treated with chlorine. Explain why chlorine is added to water even though it is toxic. Give an equation for the reaction of chlorine with cold water.

[3 marks]

• Reason: sterilise water / disinfect water / kill bacteria / kill microorganisms / kill microbes
• Explanation: health benefit outweighs risk / only used in small quantities/low concentrations
• Equation: Cl2 + H2O <=> HCl + HClO
Also accept: 2 Cl2 + 2 H2O -> 4 HCl + O2
AQA-7405.R_3_2_3_CHLORINE_WATER_EQUATION_REASON

Give an equation for the reaction of chlorine with water. Give a reason why chlorine is added to drinking water.

[2 marks]

• Cl2 + H2O <=> HCl + HClO / 2 Cl2 + 2 H2O -> 4 HCl + O2
• Kills bacteria / kills microorganisms / kills microbes / kills pathogens
Also accept: sterilise water / disinfect water
AQA-7405.R_3_2_3_CHLORINE_ACIDIC_SOLUTION_EQUATION

Give an equation to show how chlorine forms an acidic solution in water.

[1 mark]

• Cl2 + H2O <=> HCl + HOCl
• Or
• 2 Cl2 + 2 H2O -> 4 HCl + O2
Also accept: ->
Also accept: multiples
AQA-7405.R_3_2_3_CHLORINE_WATER_REDOX_ELECTRONS

Give an equation for the reaction of chlorine with water to form a solution containing two acids. Explain, with reference to electrons, why this is a redox reaction.

[2 marks]

• Cl2 + H2O -> HCl + HClO
• chlorine/Cl/Cl2 gains electron(s) (to form Cl-) **and** loses electron(s) (to form ClO-)
Also accept: Cl2 + H2O -> 2 H+ + Cl- + ClO-
Ignore: chlorine is oxidised and reduced
Ignore: disproportionation
Ignore: oxidation numbers unless incorrect
AQA-7405.R_3_2_3_CHLORINE_COLD_NAOH_BLEACH

Give an equation for the reaction between chlorine and cold, dilute aqueous sodium hydroxide.

[1 mark]

Cl2 + 2 NaOH -> NaCl + NaOCl + H2O
Also accept: multiples
AQA-7405.R_3_2_3_NACL_CONC_H2SO4_EQUATION_ACID_ROLE

Solid sodium chloride reacts with concentrated sulfuric acid. Give an equation for this reaction. State the role of the sulfuric acid in this reaction.

[2 marks]

• NaCl + H2SO4 -> NaHSO4 + HCl
• Proton donor
Also accept: 2 NaCl + H2SO4 -> Na2SO4 + 2 HCl
Also accept: (Bronsted-Lowry) acid
AQA-7405.R_3_2_3_NACL_CONC_H2SO4_CHLORIDE_ROLE

Give the equation for the reaction of solid sodium chloride with concentrated sulfuric acid. State the role of the chloride ions in this reaction.

[2 marks]

• NaCl + H2SO4 -> HCl + NaHSO4
• or
• 2 NaCl + H2SO4 -> 2 HCl + Na2SO4
• base/proton acceptor
AQA-7405.R_3_2_3_HALIDE_NO_REDOX_CONC_H2SO4

Some solid sodium halides react with concentrated sulfuric acid without any redox reaction taking place. Identify a sodium halide that behaves in this way. Give an equation for the reaction. State the role of the halide ion in this reaction.

[3 marks]

• (Sodium) fluoride or (sodium) chloride
• NaCl + H2SO4 -> HCl + NaHSO4
• OR
• NaF + H2SO4 -> HF + NaHSO4
• Base / proton acceptor
Also accept: equations to form SO4 2- ions
Also accept: 2 NaCl + H2SO4 -> 2 HCl + Na2SO4
Also accept: 2 NaF + H2SO4 -> 2 HF + Na2SO4
Also accept: ionic equations
AQA-7405.R_3_2_3_HALIDE_REDUCES_H2SO4_TO_H2S

A halide ion X- reduces concentrated sulfuric acid to hydrogen sulfide. Identify the halide ion. Give an equation for the reaction.

[2 marks]

• I- or iodide
• H2SO4 + 8 H+ + 8 I- -> H2S + 4 H2O + 4 I2
Also accept: astatide
Also accept: multiples
Also accept: 8 HI
Also accept: 10 H+ + SO4 2- + 8 I- -> H2S + 4 H2O + 4 I2
AQA-7405.R_3_2_3_CL2_WITH_IODIDE_OBSERVATION

A student bubbles chlorine gas through a solution of sodium iodide. State the observation the student would make. Give an ionic equation for the reaction.

[2 marks]

• brown solution **or** black solid (forms)
• Cl2 + 2 I- -> 2 Cl- + I2
Also accept: multiples
Not accepted: purple
Ignore: state symbols
AQA-7405.R_3_2_3_IODIDE_CONC_H2SO4_TWO_PRODUCTS

A student adds a few drops of concentrated sulfuric acid to a small amount of solid sodium iodide. Two gaseous sulfur-containing products are formed. Give an equation for the formation of each of these sulfur-containing products. State the role of sulfuric acid in the formation of these products.

[3 marks]

• H2SO4 + 2 H+ + 2 I- -> SO2 + 2 H2O + I2
• H2SO4 + 8 H+ + 8 I- -> H2S + 4 H2O + 4 I2
• oxidising agent
Also accept: SO42- + 4 H+ + 2 I- -> SO2 + 2 H2O + I2
Also accept: SO42- + 10 H+ + 8 I- -> H2S + 4 H2O + 4 I2
Also accept: equations can be in either order
Also accept: alternative correct balanced equations starting from NaI to form SO2 and H2S eg 2 H2SO4 + 2 NaI -> Na2SO4 + SO2 + 2 H2O + I2
Also accept: 3 H2SO4 + 2 NaI -> 2 NaHSO4 + SO2 + 2 H2O + I2
Also accept: 5 H2SO4 + 8 NaI -> 4 Na2SO4 + H2S + 4 H2O + 4 I2
Also accept: 9 H2SO4 + 8 NaI -> 8 NaHSO4 + H2S + 4 H2O + 4 I2
AQA-7405.R_3_2_3_AGNO3_WITH_FLUORIDE

State what is observed when silver nitrate solution is added to sodium fluoride solution.

[1 mark]

Colourless (solution)
Also accept: no (visible) change, no reaction or no ppt (formed)
Ignore: none or nothing
AQA-7405.R_3_2_3_TEST_HYDROXIDE_IONS

Describe a test to confirm that a solution contains hydroxide ions.

[1 mark]

• (Add) universal indicator and it turns blue / purple
• or
• (Add) red litmus and it turns blue
Also accept: Add a named soluble magnesium salt and (slight) white precipitate formed
AQA-7405.R_3_2_3_NABR_CONC_H2SO4_BROMINE

Give an equation for the reaction of solid sodium bromide with concentrated sulfuric acid to form bromine. State one observation made during this reaction.

[2 marks]

• 2H2SO4 + 2NaBr -> Na2SO4 + SO2 + Br2 + 2H2O
• orange/brown fumes/solution
Also accept: ionic and equation forming NaHSO4
Also accept: 3H2SO4 + 2NaBr -> 2NaHSO4 + SO2 + Br2 + 2H2O
Also accept: 2H+ + 2Br- + H2SO4 -> SO2 + Br2 + 2H2O
Not accepted: equation from HBr unless formation of HBr shown in separate equation
Not accepted: liquid / yellow solid / bad eggs smell / white ppt
Ignore: choking gas/fumes / steamy/white fumes
AQA-7405.R_3_2_6_ALCL3_WATER_COMPLEX_EQUATION

When anhydrous aluminium chloride reacts with water, solution Y is formed that contains a complex aluminium ion, Z, and chloride ions. Give an equation for this reaction.

[1 mark]

AlCl3 + 6H2O -> [Al(H2O)6]3+ + 3Cl-
Also accept: AlCl3 + 6H2O -> Al(H2O)5(OH)2+ + H+ + 3Cl-
Also accept: equation to form Al(H2O)4(OH)2+
AQA-7405.R_3_2_6_AL2SO43_WATER_EQUATION

When anhydrous aluminium sulfate, Al2(SO4)3, is added to water a solution forms that contains the complex aluminium ion, [Al(H2O)6]3+ Give the equation for the reaction.

[1 mark]

Al2(SO4)3 + 12 H2O -> 2 [Al(H2O)6]3+ + 3 SO42-
Also accept: [Al(H2O)6]2(SO4)3
AQA-7405.R_3_2_6_AL_AQUA_ION_ACIDIC

Explain why the solution containing [Al(H2O)6]3+ is acidic.

[2 marks]

• Al3+ has a high charge **and** small size
• OR
• Al3+ has a high charge density
• Al3+ weakens the O-H bond (in water ligands and donates H+ to water or forms H3O+ ions with water)
